fixes.swift_fix: Use explicit do/catch/finally cleanup pattern with structured error handling
fixes.risk: Resource leak - buffers not returned to pool. Fire-and-forget Task in defer may never execute if actor is deallocated or task is cancelled.
fixes.swift_principle: defer blocks execute synchronously. async Task in defer = fire-and-forget with no completion guarantee. In actors, these orphaned Tasks may never execute.

fixes.issue: [weak self] in actor prevents progress updates
fixes.swift_fix: Remove [weak self] - actors don't need weak capture for isolated methods
fixes.risk: Progress updates lost - user sees stuck UI at 60%. Self is captured but [weak self] pattern from classes incorrectly applied to actor.
fixes.swift_principle: Actors have different memory model than classes. [weak self] in actor closures prevents proper self capture, causing silent failures. Use [self] for strong capture or rely on implicit capture for Sendable closures.

fixes.risk: Race condition - manual flag not synchronized with actor isolation. May miss cancellation signals or continue executing after cancel() called.
fixes.swift_principle: Manual cancellation flags are unsafe in concurrent contexts. Task provides built-in cooperative cancellation: Task.isCancelled (property), Task.checkCancellation() (throws), withCheckedContinuation(checkingCancellation:). These integrate with Swift's structured concurrency.

additional_findings.issue: [weak self] in actor Task closure may cause transcription result to be lost
additional_findings.swift_fix: Use [self] for strong capture - actor ensures proper isolation
additional_findings.risk: Transcription task completes but self has become nil, result lost
additional_findings.swift_principle: Inside actor-isolated code, self is always valid. [weak self] introduces unnecessary nil-checking and potential data loss.

additional_findings.issue: AsyncStream termination not explicitly handled in StreamingSpeechProcessor
additional_findings.current_code: // AsyncStream used but no explicit termination handling in transcribeChunk
additional_findings.swift_fix: Use for-await with explicit termination or Task.withCheckedThrowingContinuation
additional_findings.risk: Stream may hang if producer stops without terminating, causing memory leak
additional_findings.swift_principle: AsyncThrowingStream requires explicit termination (continuation.finish() or continuation.yield with error) or the consumer may await indefinitely.

swift_concurrency_principles: defer executes synchronously - never use async Task inside
Actors have value-semantics for isolation - [weak self] is usually wrong
Always pair buffer acquisition with guaranteed release (defer only for sync cleanup)
